lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: linear versus nonlinear patterns

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt:
A table shows:
x: 0, 1, 2, 3
y: 2, 5, 8, 11
Is the relationship linear or nonlinear?

steps: Find the differences between consecutive y-values: 5 - 2 = 3, 8 - 5 = 3, 11 - 8 = 3.
The first differences are all equal to 3.
A constant first difference means the relationship is linear.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Classify the equation y = 9x + 12 as linear or nonlinear.
choices: cannot be determined from an equation

items.prompt: A function contains the points (-4, 14) and (-8, 46). Write the function rule f(x) = mx + b.
A taxi charges a $106 flat fee plus $12 per mile. Which function models the total fare f(x) for x miles?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An elevator waits on the ground floor, then rises steadily to the top floor. Which description best matches the shape of the graph over time?
choices: decreasing at a constant rate the whole time
increasing at a constant rate the whole time

items.prompt:
A graph shows height over time.
From t = 0 to t = 1, height goes from 16 to 16.
From t = 1 to t = 6, height goes from 16 to 17.
From t = 6 to t = 11, height goes from 17 to 16.
Which interval shows the height decreasing?
Consider the relation {(2, -15), (-8, 12), (-11, 4), (-8, -3)}. Is this relation a function?
choices: It is a function only if every output is different.
No, this relation is not a function.
Cannot be determined from the given pairs.
Yes, this relation is a function.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: Which set of ordered pairs does NOT represent a function?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
